_comment: THE POPULATIONS OF THIS REPOSITORY'S COMMITTED `.ct` CORPUS, each with the
producer that writes it and the remedy when it goes stale against that producer.
Read by `tools/chain/ct-corpus-census.mjs`. A tracked `.ct` path that matches no
population below is a FAILURE and not an 'other': an unclassified corpus arriving
quietly is precisely how the hand censuses in `codetracer-specs`'
CTFS-Reader-Revision-Rollout went wrong, once on the population (a `find` counted
generated copies under `client/dist/` as committed) and once on the PRODUCER (all 52
containers were described as chain recordings needing a node and a replay driver,
when ten of them are `nargo trace` recordings of local Noir packages whose sources are
vendored beside them and whose re-record command is committed).
`producer` is the thing that must be run to re-record the population. It is the field
that decides the remedy, and grouping by it is what makes the two halves of this
corpus distinguishable: every chain recording is at container version 3 and every
`nargo trace` one is at 5, and no amount of looking at the version byte alone says why.

chain: BLOCKED on a producer bump in a repository that is not in this workspace, and the
blocker was measured rather than assumed on 2026-10-04.
The producer is `metacraft-labs/aztec-avm-runtime`'s replay driver plus
`aztec_ct_writer.wasm`. The built writer available here is
/nix/store/2akip1fivva63rh4g3577wj8yaynb2l7-aztec-ct-writer-wasm-0.0.0, and its own
build inputs say what it emits:
the wasm's source derivation materialises `codetracer-trace-format` at
592fa42cbfd759cf13398180798daaf856eb7e9d (it writes that SHA into
`build-wasm-deps/materialised-at`), and at that revision
`codetracer_ctfs/src/header.rs` declares `pub const VERSION: u8 = 3` and
`codetracer_trace_writer/src/meta_dat.rs` declares
`pub const META_DAT_VERSION: u16 = 3`.
So re-recording the chain corpus with the PINNED producer reproduces exactly the
state that makes it unreadable: container version 3, `meta.dat` schema 3. The real
prerequisite is a `pins.json` bump of the `trace_format` and `trace_format_nim`
anchors in `aztec-avm-runtime` and a rebuild of the writer wasm, which is work in
that repository and not in this one.
SUPERSEDED IN PART ON 2026-10-14, and the correction is recorded rather than
overwritten, because the paragraph above is still the right account of what THIS
repository builds and only its last sentence has expired.
THE UPSTREAM BUMP HAPPENED. `metacraft-labs/aztec-avm-runtime`'s `pins.json` on
`agents` (a94fdde, the merge of PR #8) declares:
trace_format            3fada0b03c3d1a0cbc7c35f278aa639028d702c5   2026-10-08
trace_format_nim        051efd22b00ec3b88676fb07755a65c5a4ca8fde   2026-10-08
trace_format_nim_writer 051efd22b00ec3b88676fb07755a65c5a4ca8fde   2026-10-08
The THIRD anchor is the one to notice: it did not exist at the revision this
repository pins, and it is the one that decides what the shipped writer emits.
`ct-writer/Cargo.toml`'s default feature is `path-b` — the NIM writer — so the
Rust `trace_format` anchor no longer answers the question this paragraph used to
answer with it.
AND WHAT THAT WRITER EMITS IS EXACTLY WHAT THE DEPLOYED ENGINE ACCEPTS. At
051efd22b0, `src/codetracer_ctfs/types.nim` declares `CtfsVersion* = 5` and
`CtfsVersionV6* = 6`; `container.nim:41` stamps `CtfsVersion` and
`compact.nim:122` stamps `image[5] = CtfsVersionV6`; and
`src/codetracer_trace_writer/meta_dat.nim:143` declares `MetaDatVersion* = 6`.
The engine pinned at `client/hydrate/engine-pin.txt` accepts container {5, 6} and
`meta.dat` [6] — see `tools/chain/health-checks.json`'s `shipped-engine`. Full and
compact both land inside it.
SO THE WRITER ANCHOR MUST BE HELD AT 051efd22b0 AND NOT ADVANCED.
`codetracer-trace-format-nim`'s own `agents` HEAD declares `MetaDatVersion* = 7`,
and the deployed engine reads 6 only. Following the branch instead of the pin
produces containers this site's own reader refuses, which is the failure the pin
exists to prevent and is the opposite of the usual direction of staleness.
WHAT IS ACTUALLY OUTSTANDING IS IN THIS REPOSITORY, and it is a BUILD rather than
a pin. Three measurements, all taken 2026-10-14:
1. `flake.nix` pins `aztec-avm-runtime` at 75d1592a3d1ab4dc795e04d931c9f268b4973835
— an ancestor of `agents`, 90 commits behind. At that revision
`ct-writer/build.rs` DOES NOT EXIST, `ct-writer/Cargo.toml` has no
`[features]` section, and `pins.json` has no `trace_format_nim_writer`
anchor. There is no Path B there to select.
2. `nix eval .#aztec-ct-writer-wasm.outPath` resolves to
/nix/store/psfzx2ww4r7ix9i8jvj9085wbdpj2a8q-aztec-ct-writer-wasm-0.0.0 —
270,669 bytes, sha256 4b51cc3642c82072…. Its export section, read with
`WebAssembly.Module.exports`, carries 39 names: 38 ABI functions plus
`memory`, and ZERO imports. `ct_writer_set_compact_threshold` is NOT among
them. aztec's `verify_all_abi_functions_served.sh` says the ABI 'was
thirty-eight until CCP-6, which added `ct_writer_set_compact_threshold`', so
the count names the revision: this is a pre-CCP-6 Path A module. Its own
`pins.json` gives Path B's shipped module as 743,420 bytes, which is the
independent check on that reading.
3. The store path the paragraph above names,
/nix/store/2akip1fivva63rh4g3577wj8yaynb2l7-…, has been collected and is
gone. A store path is a measurement's receipt and not a durable citation;
the derivation attribute is, which is why (2) names the attribute first.
THE WRITER THIS REPOSITORY BUILDS TODAY THEREFORE CANNOT EMIT A COMPACT
CONTAINER, and no re-record from it can. That is measured on the module, not
inferred from the pins.
THE REMAINING WORK, NAMED SO IT IS NOT RE-DERIVED:
a. Bump `flake.nix`'s `aztec-avm-runtime` input to `agents` (a94fdde or later),
which is where `--compact-threshold` is reachable from
`replay/tools/replay_settled_transaction.mjs`.
b. Teach `tools/chain/nix/default.nix`'s `ctWriterWasm` to build Path B. It
materialises the RUST half only (`traceFormatSrc` into
`build-wasm-deps/ctf`) and runs a bare `cargo build`, which at the bumped
revision selects `path-b` by default and then needs what `build.rs` needs:
a `codetracer-trace-format-nim` OBJECT STORE at the
`trace_format_nim_writer` anchor (there is an env hook,
`CT_TRACE_FORMAT_NIM_REPO`), a libzstd cross-built for
`wasm32-unknown-unknown`, and `nim` at the version `pins.json` declares.
The obstacle that is not a missing input: `build.rs` resolves clang,
llvm-ar, lld and the wasi-libc headers by SHELLING OUT to
`nix build --inputs-from`, which cannot run inside a nix sandbox. That
wants an env override upstream, in the shape `CT_TRACE_FORMAT_NIM_REPO`
already has, rather than a patch carried here.
c. Thread `--compact-threshold` through `tools/chain/lib/replay.mjs`'s
`replayTransaction` argv (the single construction point) and out to
`capture-chain.mjs` / `follow-chain.mjs`.
d. Gate it: assert the built module's export set contains
`ct_writer_set_compact_threshold`, and that a container it writes has byte 5
= 6 with the profile byte at offset 16 = 1. An unchecked wasm rebuild is how
(2) above came to be believed to be something else.
THE BODIES ARE NOT THE BLOCKER, and that is worth recording because
`tools/chain/record-noir-frames-fixture.mjs`'s header says they are: 'the node serves
transaction bodies only out of its active pool, for about an hour, and that hour is
long gone'. True of the node and not of the corpus. Measured on 2026-10-04 against
the first transaction of `client/fixtures/chain/aztec-testnet/snapshot.json`
the keyless file store answered HTTP 200 with 195116 bytes whose leading 32 bytes
ARE the requested hash, so the payload self-verified against its own key;
a fabricated hash 404ed and a wrong base path 404ed, so the 200 is measured
against two failures;
the node answered `null` to BOTH `node_getTxByHash` and `node_getTxEffect` — a
stronger control than ING-4's 'refused with the pool-pruned reason', because the
testnet has since been REDEPLOYED (the snapshot's rollup is
0xd73a91bdcf6891c7642f3e460036e1ef2cc23178 at rollupVersion 1821665230; the live
node reports 0x8c2fb2a68a3d362ab1de99e06f83f8903160bbd9 at 2914217885, tip 8150),
so the whole deployment is gone from the node and the store is the only surviving
source.
NOTHING COSTS ANYTHING WHILE THIS IS OPEN. No gate depends on any chain container
being readable: `chain-health.mjs` reports them as `H-CONTAINER-UNREADABLE`
findings, which is the tool working, and the committed reading at
`tools/chain/measurements/chain-health.json` records that figure.
restampingIsForbidden: Flipping the `meta.dat` schema byte on these containers is NOT an option, and the
reason is this format's own history rather than a policy preference. A schema-3
writer packed a line-only `global_position_index` as `prefixSum[path_id] + line`;
schema 4 on packs `prefixSum[path_id] + (line - 1)`. Both land inside the trace's
own address space and nothing else in the container tells them apart, so a reader
that accepted a schema-3 container would place every step one line high AND report
success. That incident is why the refusal exists.
Nor is vouching per read, and that one is no longer merely discouraged — it is
